cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he opens with a big question for the LORD: who may abide in His tent and dwell on His holy mountain? Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. You had me at "tent."

cards.question: David asks the LORD who may dwell on His holy mountain. True or false: David answers with a list of offerings to bring to the LORD's tent.

cards.text: First, the big picture: this person walks with integrity and practices righteousness. He's the SAME GUY in the meeting as he is in the parking lot when somebody takes his spot.

cards.question: David says the person who walks with integrity speaks the truth from his heart. What kind of honesty is that?

answers.text: Honesty that goes all the way down
Honesty that waits for the right crowd
Honesty that kicks in under pressure

cards.text: Then David turns to the tongue, and this person has no slander on it. He has never once sent the group chat text that starts with "I'm not trying to start anything, BUT…"

cards.question: David says the one who dwells on the LORD's holy mountain does no harm to his neighbor.
No slander on his tongue, no harm to his neighbor, no scorn on his friend. Who are all three of these about?

cards.text: Next, David gets to who this person looks up to. He despises the vile, so he is NOT out here giving the troublemakers a standing ovation.

cards.question: The one who despises the vile honors a different kind of person instead. Who?

cards.text: Now the tough one: this person made an oath, and it turns out to be a costly one. Like saying "Sure, I'll help you move" and THEN finding out it's a third floor walk-up with no elevator.

cards.question: Once his oath starts costing him, the person in Psalm 15 revises it.

cards.text: Then David gets to the wallet: what this person does when he lends his money. This is right about where a lot of us start studying the ceiling real hard.

cards.question: When the one who dwells on the LORD's holy mountain lends his money, he lends it without ___.

cards.text: Then David brings up a bribe, money to turn this person against the innocent. I'd love to tell you I've never been tempted, but you wave a bag of chocolate chips at me and I start NEGOTIATING.

cards.question: When a bribe comes against the innocent, the one who dwells on the LORD's holy mountain ___ it.

cards.text: And David brings it home. After that whole list, he has one last word about the one who does these things.

cards.question: What does David say about the one who does these things?
